facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 10:00 AM ET

The defending NBA Cup champions are heading home early.

The New York Knicks lost 108-105 to Miami on Black Friday, finishing Cup group play at 1-3 and missing the knockout round entirely. Giannis Antetokounmpo made sure of it — the Heat's superstar delivered 22 points and 23 rebounds in what has to be one of the great individual performances in group-play history.

The Philadelphia 76ers won East Group B on the head-to-head tiebreaker over Miami, meaning the Heat are also out despite winning the game that mattered most. Only in a tiebreaker situation could you beat your rival, win the game, and still miss the bracket.

For the Knicks, it's a stunning reversal. They were Cup champions just a year ago. Now they're watching from the couch in December.

The good news for New York: they've been playing excellent regular-season basketball. The Cup is gone. The playoffs are still very much in reach.

Stephon Castle is making a serious statement.

The second-year Spur dropped 26 points on Friday night as San Antonio edged the Los Angeles Lakers 99-96 in the NBA Cup Black Friday nightcap, clinching the West wild card and sending the Lakers home. Victor Wembanyama backed him up with 25 points and 16 rebounds.

The Spurs are in the quarterfinals. They'll face the Dallas Mavericks — the only 4-0 team in all of group play — in what promises to be one of the week's best matchups when the knockout round tips off Dec. 4.

Castle was a lottery pick just two drafts ago. Now he's delivering in Cup-clinching moments on national television. He's going to be very, very good.

Hawks 87, Celtics 86. One of the grittiest Cup games of group play. Atlanta wins East Group C (3-1). Boston also 3-1 but enters as wild card. These two meet again Dec 4-5 — from different seeds. #NBA

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 1:00 PM ET

Eighty-seven to eighty-six.

That was the final score when the Atlanta Hawks beat the Boston Celtics in one of the gritiest Cup group-play games of the year. Both teams finished 3-1 in East Group C, but Atlanta won the group on tiebreaker. Boston enters as the East wild card — meaning these two teams could potentially meet again later in the knockout round.

It was a defensive grind from start to finish, the kind of game you usually only see in the playoffs. The Hawks earned it. Boston earned a second chance.
